semantics: Each floor is a red line. For any snapshot whose computed fields match a floor's condition at or beyond applies_age_months_gte (corrected age where weeks_early > 3 and age < 24m), the compiled report's severity must be at least min_severity. Severity order: none < watch < discuss < priority_discuss. The interpretation artifact may flag earlier or harder than a floor, never later or softer. The floors grader enforces this at compile time by evaluating the interpretation artifact against a generated case grid; any floor-matching case that compiles below min_severity fails the build.
fields_contract: Conditions reference only computable snapshot fields: vocab_says (int), vocab_understands (int), and the 12 behavior items by id with values yes | sometimes | not_yet (lost_skills uses yes | no). 'not_yet' matches only 'not_yet'; 'sometimes' never satisfies an absence condition.

floors.rationale: Loss of previously acquired words or skills at any age is the single most established red flag in the early identification literature and short-circuits every other consideration.
Consistent non-response to name by 12 months is an established early social-communication flag and also a hearing flag; the guidance block must mention both routes.
No gesturing (waving, reaching to be picked up, pointing to request) by 12 months, encoded as absence of both gesture items.
Declarative pointing (to share interest, not only to request) is expected by 12-15 months; its absence at 15 months warrants a conversation. Floor set at the outer bound of the settled range.

No single words by 16 months, the canonical absolute threshold. Word approximations used consistently count as words per instrument instructions, which keeps this floor conservative in the right direction.
Fewer than 50 expressive words or no two-word combinations at 24 months, the standard late-talker identification criterion. Note the OR: either condition alone triggers.

Not following simple one-step directions without gesture cues by 24 months flags receptive language, which is easy for expressive-focused tools to miss. Receptive concerns are, if anything, more predictive than expressive ones.

Policy floor, enforced by lexicon grader rather than case grid: no interpretation output may soften or delay any floor above on the basis of multilingual exposure. Bilingual children hit these floors on total-across-languages counts (the instrument already counts any language), and 'wait because bilingual' is a documented driver of late referral. Guidance may add bilingual context; it may never downgrade severity.
